fact_previews: PCR data indicates that IL-10@NPs can enhance the immune response within tumors in situ liver cancer by increasing the expression of granzyme (Gzmb), IFN-γ (Ifng), TNF-α (Tnfa), and programmed death receptor (Fasl).
Tumor immune slice results show that IL-10@NPs can increase the infiltration of CD8 cells and the expression of granzyme and IFN-γ in tumors of in situ liver cancer.
IL-10@NPs can be combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4) for joint treatment of mid-to-late stage in situ liver cancer.
The results indicate that the treatment effect of a single immune checkpoint inhibitor is weak, and liver cancer cells exhibit low immune responsiveness (cold tumor).
Single IL-10@NPs has a certain tumor suppression effect, but the overall effect is not satisfactory.
